messages:
marie (PM): quick heads-up — FinEdge (pilot customer) just asked if we can commit to a 50ms p95 for short prompts (<=64 tokens) for their production cutover. they want this as an SLA add-on for their paid pilot.
jonas (Eng): whoa, 50ms p95 is tight on current stack for anything non-trivial. is this for hosted only or for their dedicated cluster?
olivia (CS): Sales says hosted first, then dedicated. FinEdge will pay for higher tier if we can guarantee it. They said their main workload is short embeddings + a few completions.
sam (Sales): Confirmed — they'll sign a 6mo pilot commitment if we can hit the SLA for the first 3 months. This is material ARR (mid-six figures).
lee (SRE): Need to quantify risk. p95 50ms implies aggressive routing + reserved capacity and maybe bypassing batching for short requests. That increases token cost. Also need an observability hook for per-tenant tail metrics.
jonas (Eng): Rough feasibility notes: we can try a short-path execution mode: 1) route <=64 token requests to a low-latency pool (smaller batch, pinned workers), 2) enable KV cache prefix hits aggressively, 3) use int8 quantized model variant. Might need Dedicated-style reservations even in hosted to guarantee isolation.
marie (PM): OK. two asks for this thread: (A) should we treat this as OKR scope add (Q2 latency objective)? (B) what is the minimal deliverable to present as an SLA that engineering can commit to in 6 weeks?
jonas (Eng): For an MVP SLA: "50ms p95 for requests <=64 tokens on model X.v1 when routed to LowLatency pool, with 99.9% availability of the pool." Implementation work: ~3 wks infra (pool + routing), ~2 wks runtime changes (short-path), ~1 wk testing + obs. That's optimistic and assumes we reuse existing fleet.
lee (SRE): Add 1 wk for chaos testing and an SLI dashboard. Also we need a fallback policy: if pool saturated, automatically route to standard pool with an SLA credit process.
sam (Sales): That fallback policy is fine as long as it's transparent in contract. We can negotiate a credit instead of hard downtime.
marie (PM): Tradeoffs: if we add this to OKRs, something else must slide. Candidate to deprioritize: "Batch Optimizer" (throughput/cost opt) or postpone "Model rollout automation" by a sprint. Thoughts?
jonas (Eng): Batch Optimizer is useful for long-term cost, but this LowLatency pool is high revenue and high priority. I'd propose swapping Batch Optimizer into backlog for Q2 and move Model rollout automation to Q3.
lee (SRE): From ops POV we need a little time to standardize tenant-level metrics. If we accept this swap, we should add a new acceptance criterion: "per-tenant p95 visibility with alerting and on-call runbook".
marie (PM): Acceptance criteria (draft): [1] 50ms p95 for <=64 token requests on specified model under normal load (measured via synthetic and canary), [2] LowLatency pool autoscaling and reserved capacity rules, [3] Per-tenant SLI dashboard and runbook, [4] Fallback routing with contractual credit.
olivia (CS): I'll prepare a customer-facing note explaining the fallback and credit. Also we should add a short security review since they'll put prod data through hosted API.
sam (Sales): I'll get verbal approval from FinEdge by EOD if we can show the acceptance criteria and a timeline of 6 weeks.
marie (PM): OK — provisional decision: move Batch Optimizer out of Q2, add LowLatency SLA initiative to OKRs as a high-priority scope transfer. @jonas can you put a short implementation plan in Confluence by EOD? @lee can you estimate SLO burden for oncall?
jonas (Eng): will do — I'll drop a Confluence doc with a rollout plan and a suggested resource list.
lee (SRE): estimating oncall: extra pager noise likely for first 4 weeks of canary. I'll add ~0.2 FTE impact to SLO cost model.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary job created: `canary-lowlatency-finedge` (weekly).
marie (PM): thanks all. If Sales gets FinEdge buy-in, we'll formalize the OKR change in next week's triage meeting. For now marking this thread as decision: proceed conditional on resource signoff and CS note. :white_check_mark:
